comparison: Both evaluate claims C1, C12, C18-C21 about HIV-1PR cleavage of CARD8. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning cleavage efficiency and noting evidence of F60L mutant cleavage in Figure 1D, suggesting human specificity should be downplayed.

Both evaluate claims C7, C13-C17 about phylogenetic evidence for F59-F60 in humans. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on alignment data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more comprehensive phylogenetic analysis and cautioning about human-specificity conclusions without further evidence.

Both evaluate claims C8-C10, C22-C25 about SIVcpz cleavage patterns. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting faint bands in Figure 2A and recommending in vitro biochemical experiments to remove background, plus additional evidence for human-specificity claims.

Both evaluate claims C2-C3, C30-C39 about cell death and IL-1β secretion. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, cautioning that PI staining is generic, effects in primed THP-1 cells were modest, and questioning whether priming requirements apply to primary macrophages.

Both evaluate claims C40-C41 about IL-1β secretion across HIV-1 strains. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes limited strain testing. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns about this finding.

Both evaluate claims C5-C6, C42-C45, C48-C49 about early vs late IL-1β responses. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED but notes mechanism for early protease release could be more direct. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, challenging that 24-hour timepoints allow viral protein production and requesting earlier timepoints or RT/integration blocks.
Both evaluate claims C46-C47 about lopinavir inhibition and Vpr independence. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriate controls. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns.

Both evaluate claims C50-C57 about F60 complementation experiments. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting only VSV-G data shown in Figures 4E-F and requesting verification with wild-type HIV-1, plus testing SIVcpz with chimpanzee CARD8.

Both evaluate claims C26-C27, C103 about SIVmac and other primate lentiviral proteases. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes limited characterization. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns about these findings.
Both evaluate claim C29 about cytoplasmic Gag processing. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on immunoblot data and cited literature. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED without challenging this finding.

OpenEval evaluates C11, C23, C85-C89 about evolutionary inference of SIVcpz cleavage capacity as SUPPORTED. Peer R11 evaluates overlapping claims C85-C89, C91-C93 as UNCERTAIN, accepting timing arguments but noting speculation about ancient infections and requesting stronger phylogenetic analysis for human-specificity claims.

OpenEval evaluates C91-C93 about ancient virus driving F60 evolution as UNCERTAIN/speculative. Peer R11 also rates overlapping evolutionary claims as UNCERTAIN, noting the speculation remains unsubstantiated and requesting more phylogenetic evidence.

OpenEval evaluates C96-C97 about pathogenic implications as SUPPORTED based on cited literature. Peer R12 evaluates overlapping pathogenesis claims (C94-C99, C104) as UNCERTAIN, stating relevance for pathogenesis remains speculative with modest effects and no evidence in primary cells with wild-type virus.

OpenEval evaluates C104 about CARD8 in macaque infections as UNCERTAIN/speculative. Peer R12 includes C104 in broader pathogenesis evaluation rated UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of evidence in relevant target cells.

OpenEval evaluates C100-C101 (among other background claims) as SUPPORTED established knowledge. Peer R13 rates C100-C101 as UNSUPPORTED, directly challenging the claim as overstatement since SIVcpz causes disease in wild chimpanzees (Keele et al., 2009).

OpenEval evaluates C4, C80 about TLR-dependent IL-1β secretion as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these claims, though peer R4 tangentially questions priming requirements.
OpenEval evaluates C75-C76, C78 about CARD8's broad viral sensing capacity as SUPPORTED, relying on cited literature. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these claims.
OpenEval evaluates C81-C83 about in vivo priming sources as UNCERTAIN/speculative. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these claims about priming mechanisms.
OpenEval evaluates C58-C74 as SUPPORTED background knowledge establishing context. No corresponding peer review result addresses these background claims.
